summary.text: Pat Fallon is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 4th Congressional District. A former Air Force officer and business owner, he served on the Frisco city council and in both chambers of the Texas Legislature before his election to Congress, where he sits on the Armed Services, Intelligence and Oversight committees and chairs the Military Personnel subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: Fallon was born in Pittsfield, Massachusetts, in 1967 and earned a degree in government and international relations from the University of Notre Dame in 1990. His official biography says he played varsity football under coach Lou Holtz and was a member of the 1988 national championship team.

He received a commission as an Air Force officer upon graduation and, according to his official biography, was stationed at Sheppard Air Force Base in Wichita Falls, Texas. He served on active duty for four years and received an honorable discharge at the rank of captain.
Fallon then worked as an entrepreneur and as president and CEO of Virtus Apparel; his official biography says he founded more than a dozen companies.

Fallon served on the Frisco city council from 2009 to 2012, including as mayor pro tem from 2011 to 2012. He served in the Texas House of Representatives (District 106) from 2013 to 2019 and in the Texas Senate (District 30) from 2019 to 2021.

He has represented Texas's 4th Congressional District since 2021, succeeding John Ratcliffe. In the 119th Congress he serves on the Armed Services Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Military Personnel, the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and the Oversight Committee.

According to his official biography, he completed the World Marathon Challenge (seven marathons on seven continents in seven days) on January 29, 2016, to raise funds and awareness for pediatric cancer research.
